title: Plex now helps sell movie theater tickets
gist: Plex partnered with Fandango to show movie-ticket purchase links on title pages for films in theaters, a move to monetize its content-discovery data beyond its media server software. The deal adds Kochava attribution so studios and advertisers can measure campaign-to-ticket conversion.

insights.claim: Plex users in the US now see a Fandango ticketing option on title pages for movies currently in theaters, linking out to Fandango for showtimes and purchases, with Kochava attribution so studios and advertisers can see how campaigns convert into ticket sales.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Plex is building an ad/attribution revenue line from discovery traffic; watch for further partner integrations.

insights.claim: Fandango sells tickets for 31,000 US movie theater screens and gets access to Plex streaming-service data, which Plex says reflects more than 100 million streaming decisions each month, including ratings and cross-platform viewing, to gauge audience intent.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Shows the scale of the audience-intent dataset Plex is trying to sell; the 100M figure is Plex's own claim.

insights.claim: Fandango frames the deal as turning discovery signals (what fans search for and watch across services) into theater visits, while giving studios and advertisers a more direct, measurable path to ticket sales.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Measurable discovery-to-purchase attribution is the product being sold to the studio ad budget.
insights.quote: Plex has a unique view into what movie fans are actively considering

themes.theme: Content discovery as a monetizable asset

insights.claim: Content discovery is a frequently cited unsolved challenge in streaming, with smart TV OS operators, streaming services and generative AI chatbots all trying to crack it, so Plex monetizing it could prove lucrative if its user data drives worthwhile recommendations.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Discovery layer competition is crowded; Plex's edge depends on recommendation quality, not just data.
insights.locator: Content discovery is a frequently cited challenge

insights.claim: Plex aims to be the place where people discover what to watch regardless of where the content lives, per co-founder and CPO Scott Olechowski.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Positions Plex as an aggregator-neutral discovery layer rather than a content owner.
insights.quote: the place where people can discover what to watch, regardless of where that content lives

insights.claim: Plex is expanding beyond its media server software into a rental streaming service (launched over two-and-a-half years ago), a free ad-supported TV (FAST) service, social features and now ticketing, adding revenue streams beyond the server product.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: The company is shifting its revenue mix toward ads and transactions rather than server licensing.
insights.locator: The foray into movie ticket sales comes over two-and-a-half years

insights.claim: Plex's media server lets users share movies they own without paying Hollywood licensing fees, which contrasts with the Fandango partnership with the movie industry; the businesses coexist and server-only users can opt out of some data sharing, though Plex says it collects data from media server users searching on Plex.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Tension between the piracy-adjacent server base and industry partnerships plus data collection is a privacy and reputation risk to monitor.

insights.claim: Plex has discussed the difficulty of making lifetime passes financially sustainable, and the new businesses may help fund media-software maintenance, although the company appears largely focused on building out the non-server aspects of the business.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Legacy lifetime-pass liabilities push Plex toward new monetization; server users may get less of its focus.
